---
title: "About"
---

::: {.site-intro}
Peekei is a data scientist working at the intersection of biostatistics, bioinformatics, and computational biology.
:::

A BSc in Biostatistics laid the foundation; the next steps are mapped out deliberately — an MSc in Molecular Biology and Bioinformatics at JKUAT, a PhD, postdoctoral research, and eventually founding a biotech startup grounded in computational biology.

This site tracks that trajectory in public. The analyses here move fluidly between **R and Python** depending on what the problem calls for — survival models and Bayesian hierarchical methods in R, machine learning and SHAP-based interpretability in Python via `reticulate`, and everything in between — written to methods-section rigor rather than tutorial simplicity. Recurring threads: survival analysis, Bayesian methods, epidemic dynamics, multi-omics integration, and machine learning applied to biological data. The goal is a portfolio that reads less like coursework and more like the working notebook of someone building toward independent research.

That same work is also packaged as reusable, CRAN-compliant R functions in [`omicsuite`](https://github.com/Real-peekei/omicsuite) — an extensible collection of pipelines for biostatistics, bioinformatics, and computational biology generally, not limited to what's covered in the articles here. Each pipeline follows the same contract: fit a model, run the diagnostic checks a careful methods section would include, and return a structured verdict table rather than a bare point estimate. Full reference and vignettes live on its own [pkgdown site](https://real-peekei.github.io/omicsuite/).
